entries.title: Acts 19:9
segments:
The Way. Christianity.
 

 
Tyrannus. Head of a school of philosophic disputants.

entries.title: Acts 19:10
segments: Fifty thousand pieces of silver. Fifty thousand drachmas.  Equal to about ten thousand dollars.

entries.title: Acts 19:13
segments: Exorcists. Who pretended to expel the evil spirits by uttering certain words alleged to have a magical effect.

entries.title: Acts 19:24
segments: Diana. A goddess personifying the fruitful powers of nature.

entries.title: Acts 19:25
segments: Workmen of like occupation. Those who were employed in the procuring and preparation of the materials used in the manufacture of the shrines.

entries.title: Acts 19:27
segments: All Asia. Contributions for the Temple were sent in from all parts of the province of Asia.

entries.title: Acts 19:33
segments: Alexander. Who was chosen as a representative Jew to convince the crowd that the Jews of Ephesus had no sympathy with Paul and his preaching.

entries.title: Acts 19:35
segments:
The town clerk. He kept the city records, received public communications, sent replies in his name in the city's behalf, and was the presiding officer at the regular popular assemblies.  He also put in writing and affixed his seal to laws of the city.
 

 
Fell down from Jupiter. This was said to quiet the crowds.  If the image fell down from Jupiter, that is, had a supernatural origin, what harm could possibly befall it by reason of this disturbance?  Jupiter, the king of their gods, could take care of his own.

entries.title: Acts 19:38
segments: Proconsuls. There was only one proconsul in the province of Asia; but the town clerk meant to refer generally to courts and proconsuls to settle disputes.  See notes on
